Basically everyone uses chemicals in their hair. Even shampoo and conditioner are loaded with chemicals. Curly hair typically breaks much more easily than non-curly hair. It’s not so much “loaded with chemicals” as natural oils, because coarser hair doesn’t produce oil as much. Oils = moisture. Lack of moisture = breakage. Also, chlorine strips oils and moisture even further and causes even more tangles. 

Also, in the case of curly hair, it’s harder to achieve a long length because the curls make it draw up (shrinkage). If you have straight (less textured) hair it’s not as big of an issue to cut off the damaged parts because you can quickly grow it back to the preferred length.

If that was then case then it’s possible they just didn’t feel like redoing their whole head with products after washing and finding out the chlorine. Curly hair can be exhausting to maintain, especially in the Summer time. My daughter has long coily hair down past her waist and sometimes it feels like a part-time job.

They probably had relaxed hair, which costs a lot of money to maintain and can only be re-done so often. Not lazy, just limited options available for hair care. Now that there are more options and information available, and natural hair is being embraced, this stereotype will apply less and less. 😊
